_comment_disk: pre_mounted_config means archinstall NEVER touches the partition table.
It reads whatever is already mounted under /mnt and installs into that.
That is the whole point: this machine keeps a second NVMe with Windows on
it, and one wrong answer in the guided installer eats it. Partitioning is
Detection is by PARTITION FLAG, not by mountpoint name. archinstall's
get_efi_partition() filters on the ESP flag in the partition table, so the
new ESP must be typecode EF00. Mount an ext4 partition at /mnt/boot and it
is silently skipped, and the bootloader step dies with 'Could not detect
EFI system partition' after the packages are already installed.
_comment_bootloader: systemd-boot, not GRUB, because the new drive has its OWN ESP -- there is
no partition shared with Windows to work around any more. That deletes the
two worst failure modes of the old GRUB setup in one go: the compiled-in
prefix pointing at the wrong directory, and the shim_lock verifier that
makes Secure Boot impossible without rebuilding the binary.
It costs one thing: Windows does NOT appear in the systemd-boot menu.
systemd-boot only scans its own ESP and XBOOTLDR, and Windows' bootmgfw.efi
is on the other disk's ESP. Windows is picked from the firmware boot menu
'removable' is parsed and stored for every bootloader, but archinstall only
ACTS on it for GRUB and Limine; _add_systemd_bootloader ignores it. It is
false here so the file does not imply something that never happens.
The NVRAM entry comes from `bootctl install` instead -- and bootctl skips
writing EFI variables, silently, when it believes it is in a container,
which arch-chroot looks like as of systemd 257. archinstall works around
that with --variables=yes and falls back to --variables=no if it errors.
The fallback leaves you with no boot entry, so VERIFY it: section 5.
uki:false is explicit because UKI changes what gets signed for Secure Boot
-- one arch-linux.efi instead of systemd-bootx64.efi plus vmlinuz-linux.
_comment_packages: openssh is here so `systemctl enable sshd` is possible before the greeter
reboot -- cheap insurance, and base does not ship it, and there is no
network to install it from if the greeter comes up black.
efibootmgr is strapped automatically by _add_systemd_bootloader, but it is
listed anyway: section 5 and section 6 both need it by hand, and relying on
a side effect of someone else's install step is how you end up without it.
os-prober is gone -- it was a GRUB mechanism for putting Windows in the
menu. systemd-boot does not use it and it would find nothing to do.
